ops.partnerAndChild: {xref} cannot be both a partner in a family and a child of it.
ops.wouldBeOwnAncestor: This would make {xref} their own ancestor: they already stand above {parent}.
ops.partnerSlotTaken: {xref} already holds the other partner slot in {family}.
audit.duplicateXref: Identifier {xref} names more than one record. Identifiers are unique across the whole dataset, not within a record type.
audit.danglingPointer.family: Family {xref} names person {pointer}, which the document does not contain.
audit.danglingPointer.individual: Person {xref} links to family {pointer}, which the document does not contain.
audit.duplicateLink.child: Family {xref} lists {pointer} as a child more than once.
audit.duplicateLink.family: Person {xref} links to family {pointer} more than once.
audit.asymmetric.partnerNoFams: Family {xref} names {pointer} as a partner, but {pointer} has no FAMS link back to it.
audit.asymmetric.childNoFamc: Family {xref} lists {pointer} as a child, but {pointer} has no FAMC link back to it.
audit.asymmetric.famcNoChil: Person {xref} links to family {pointer} as a child, but {pointer} has no CHIL pointer back.
audit.asymmetric.famsNoPartner: Person {xref} links to family {pointer} as a partner, but {pointer} names neither HUSB nor WIFE pointing back.
audit.descentCycle: Person {xref} is their own ancestor. No tree can be drawn through that, so it is a fault in the links rather than an unusual family.
audit.childOfSeveralFamilies: Person {xref} is a child of {count} families ({families}). That is legal -- a birth family and an adoptive one, for instance -- and worth confirming.
audit.unconnectedPerson: Person {xref} belongs to no family. Not necessarily wrong -- a person is added before they are linked -- but a lone record is often a link that was lost.
export.phraseDropped: GEDCOM 5.5.1 has no PHRASE structure; the phrase under {under} was not written.
export.sexXDowngraded: GEDCOM 5.5.1 has no SEX value X; U was written, which says less.
export.versionRewritten: The header declared GEDCOM {declared}; {dialect} was written instead.
export.charDropped: GEDCOM 7 removed HEAD.CHAR; the declaration was dropped and the file is UTF-8.
export.charRewritten: HEAD.CHAR was rewritten to {encoding}, which is what the bytes are.
export.submitterMissing: GEDCOM 5.5.1 requires HEAD.SUBM and this document has no submitter. None was invented.
import.noVersion: Header declares no GEDCOM version; the dialect was inferred.
import.noXref: Record has no cross-reference identifier and cannot be kept; dropped.
